title: Temptation of Christ
definition: The temptation of Christ is the truth that Jesus was truly tempted yet remained completely without sin.
summary: Jesus faced real temptation and overcame without sin.
christFocus: Christ's victory in temptation qualifies Him to sympathize with and help His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus was truly tempted. His temptation was not pretend, shallow, or meaningless. Yet He never sinned in desire, thought, word, or action.

In the wilderness, Jesus resisted Satan with Scripture, trust, and submission to the Father. Where Adam failed and Israel failed, Christ obeyed.

Because He has been tempted without sin, Jesus is a merciful and faithful Savior who helps those who are tempted.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Believers often feel alone or ashamed when tempted. The temptation of Christ matters because the sinless Savior understands temptation and provides help.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Run to Christ when tempted. Use Scripture, pray quickly, resist compromise, and remember that your High Priest gives mercy and help.
